- Then the coding harness should use gemini 3.8 flash to create this world. I was thinking about using open code maybe?
- The agent should first check whether this world exists or not
- The agent should then create this world for 4 difficulty levels. It should copy the template and start modifying the files until the world is ready to be played
- An example of how such a expert mode of a world could look like (in terms of things) is here: https://foodtruckbench.com/
- I would like maybe that there is a demand componenty that is part of these worlds and is somewhere in this world like [Image #1]
- The agent should use the UI components provided and roughly use the same style
- The agent should also be able to test the world in a sandbox (it needs tests that pass until the world is live).
- Once it's live, the UI of the web app should somehow update and the world should be playable by a human (and later also an agent)

# PlanWorldSimulator world generator

Describe a planning benchmark in plain language and generate a playable world from it.
See [docs/design-decisions](docs/design-decisions) for the architecture.

The generator is a fake for now: it walks through the real steps (storyline, copy
template, fill template, tests) and writes a world folder, but does no LLM work.

## Layout

| Path                  | What it is                                                  |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/web`             | Website (Vite, React, TypeScript, Tailwind)                 |
| `src/backend`         | API (FastAPI, SQLite via SQLAlchemy and Alembic)            |
| `src/worlds-template` | Base template every world is copied from                    |
| `src/worlds`          | Generated worlds, one folder each (contents are gitignored) |

## Run it

```sh
just up      # build, start in the background, wait until healthy
just down    # stop (database and generated worlds are kept)
```

Open http://localhost:8480 (API docs on http://localhost:8400/docs). If another program uses
those ports, `just up` says so; set `PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_WEB_PORT` and
`PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_API_PORT` in `.env` to change them. Other commands: `just build`, `just logs [service]`,
`just ps`, `just reset` (also deletes the database volume) and `just dev` (live
reload, site on http://localhost:5173). Copy `.env.example` to `.env` to change
defaults.

## Develop

Needs [pixi](https://pixi.sh), [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) and [just](https://just.systems).

```sh
just install
just format
just lint
just typecheck
just test
```

# World template

The base every world is copied from. As shipped it runs a placeholder "Example world".
Full reference world: `src/worlds/bike-factory`.

```bash
pixi run dev    # server on $PORT (default 8000: REST /api, MCP /mcp) + UI on $UI_PORT (default 5173)
pixi run test   # backend tests
```

## Files

`[base]` = same in every world, never edited · `[gen]` = written per world

| File | |
|---|---|
| `pixi.toml`, `process-compose.yaml` | [base] dependencies, tasks, processes |
| `brief.md` | [gen] public story, goal, actions (given to the agent) |
| `secret.md` | [gen] hidden rules and scoring (never given to the agent) |
| `sim/env.py` | [gen] Gymnasium env + world contract (below) |
| `sim/rules.py` | [gen] dynamics and hidden rules |
| `sim/helpers.py` | [base] observation → JSON, `register_world` |
| `server/api.py` | [base] FastAPI app, generic `Game`, `/api` routes, `/mcp` mount |
| `server/mcp.py` | [gen] `build_mcp(game) -> FastMCP` with the world's tools |
| `ui/src/World.tsx` | [gen] world view and controls config; the rest of `ui/` is [base] |
| `tests/backend/test_rules.py` | [gen] world invariants; all other tests are [base] |

## Contracts

**`sim/env.py`** — one `gymnasium.Env` subclass, registered with `register_world(EnvClass)`.

- `NAME`, `DIFFICULTIES`, `__init__(difficulty)`, `actions` (tuple of world verbs).
- Difficulty fixes the structure and the `Dict` spaces; `reset(seed)` only draws values. Same seed + actions → same trace.
- `step` = one week; reward = the week's profit; `info` may carry `discovered: list[str]` and `story: {tag, text, tone}`.
- `check_action(verb, args) -> dict` — validate and normalise; raise `ValueError` if invalid.
- `encode_actions([(verb, args), ...]) -> action` — merge a week's queued actions.
- `observe(site=None) -> dict` — visible state only.
- `score() -> dict` — at least `score` (0–1), `week`, `done`.
- `baseline_action() -> action` — naive policy for the baseline score.
- `ui_state(ctx) -> dict` — at least `world {name, seed, difficulty}` and `week`; **same shape as `mockState` in `World.tsx`**. `ctx` has `seed`, `story`, `discoveries`, `active`, `queued`, `agent`.

**`server/mcp.py`** — `build_mcp(game)`. Core tools `brief`, `observe`, `note`, `advance`, `score`, plus one tool per verb in `env.actions`. Each tool calls `game.*(…, source="agent")`.

**`ui/src/World.tsx`** — exports `mockState`, `toControls(state, selectedId)`, `WorldView({ state, selectedId, onSelect })`. Draw with `shared/kit` (see `shared/kit/README.md`).

## Server

| Route | |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/state` | `env.ui_state(...)` |
| `POST /api/action {id, args}` | world verb (queued) or UI control: `play`, `fast`, `pause`, `stats`, `new_world`, `mode {mode}` |
| `POST /api/advance {steps?}` | apply queued actions and step |
| `POST /api/reset {seed?, difficulty?}` | new episode |
| `GET /api/events?after=` · `WS /api/events` | event log: MCP calls, UI actions, advances |
| `/mcp` | MCP, streamable HTTP |
"""[gen] TODO: replace with this world's Gymnasium env (contract: README.md).

Placeholder world so the template runs: one shop, invest to grow capacity,
sell to a demand drawn from the seed. One step = one week.
Reference implementation: src/worlds/bike-factory/sim/env.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import gymnasium as gym
import numpy as np
from gymnasium import spaces

from sim import rules as R
from sim.helpers import obs_to_json, register_world


class ExampleEnv(gym.Env):
    NAME = "Example world"
    DIFFICULTIES = ("easy", "medium", "hard")
    metadata = {"render_modes": []}

    def __init__(self, difficulty: str = "medium"):
        if difficulty not in self.DIFFICULTIES:
            raise ValueError(f"difficulty must be one of {self.DIFFICULTIES}")
        self.difficulty = difficulty
        self.actions: tuple[str, ...] = ("invest",)  # world verbs = MCP action tools
        self.site_ids = ["shop"]
        # Difficulty fixes the structure and the spaces.
        self.action_space = spaces.Dict({"invest": spaces.Discrete(R.MAX_INVEST + 1)})
        self.observation_space = spaces.Dict({
            "week": spaces.Discrete(R.WEEKS + 1),
            "cash": spaces.Box(-R.BIG, R.BIG, shape=(1,), dtype=np.float64),
            "capacity": spaces.Box(0, R.BIG, shape=(1,), dtype=np.float64),
            "demand": spaces.Box(0, R.BIG, shape=(1,), dtype=np.float64),
        })
        self.w: R.WorldState | None = None

    # ---------- Gymnasium API ----------

    def reset(self, *, seed: int | None = None, options: dict | None = None):
        super().reset(seed=seed)
        self.w = R.initial_state(self.np_random, self.difficulty)  # seed only draws values
        return self._obs(), {}

    def step(self, action: dict[str, Any]):
        assert self.w is not None, "call reset() first"
        reward = R.step_world(self.np_random, self.w, int(action["invest"]))
        return self._obs(), float(reward), self.w.week >= R.WEEKS, False, {"discovered": [], "story": None}

    def _obs(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        w = self.w
        assert w is not None
        f = lambda v: np.array([v], dtype=np.float64)  # noqa: E731
        return {"week": int(w.week), "cash": f(w.cash), "capacity": f(w.capacity), "demand": f(w.demand)}

    # ---------- world contract used by server/api.py ----------

    def check_action(self, verb: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if verb not in self.actions:
            raise ValueError(f"'{verb}' is not available; actions: {', '.join(self.actions)}")
        amount = args.get("amount", 1)
        if not isinstance(amount, int) or not 1 <= amount <= R.MAX_INVEST:
            raise ValueError(f"invest needs amount between 1 and {R.MAX_INVEST}")
        return {"amount": amount}

    def encode_actions(self, queued: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"invest": min(R.MAX_INVEST, sum(a["amount"] for _, a in queued))}

    def baseline_action(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"invest": 1}

    def observe(self, site: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return obs_to_json(self._obs(), self.site_ids)

    def score(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        w = self.w
        assert w is not None
        profit = w.cash - R.START_CASH
        return {"score": round(float(np.clip(profit / R.TARGET, 0, 1)), 4), "profit": round(profit),
                "week": min(w.week + 1, R.WEEKS), "done": w.week >= R.WEEKS}

    def ui_state(self, ctx: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Same shape as `mockState` in ui/src/World.tsx."""
        w = self.w
        assert w is not None
        sc = self.score()
        return {
            "world": {"name": self.NAME, "seed": str(ctx.get("seed", "")), "difficulty": self.difficulty.title()},
            "week": sc["week"],
            "weeks": R.WEEKS,
            "cash": int(w.cash),
            "capacity": int(w.capacity),
            "demand": int(w.demand),
            "profit": sc["profit"],
            "target": R.TARGET,
            "story": ctx.get("story"),
            "discoveries": {"total": 0, "found": ctx.get("discoveries", []), "hidden": []},
            "agent": ctx.get("agent", {}),
            "active": ctx.get("active"),
            "queued": ctx.get("queued", []),
            "done": sc["done"],
        }


register_world(ExampleEnv)

Reference implementation: src/worlds/bike-factory/sim/rules.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

WEEKS = 12
MAX_INVEST = 10
START_CASH = 1000.0
TARGET = 2000.0
BIG = 1e9
PRICE, INVEST_COST = 10.0, 50.0


@dataclass
class WorldState:
    week: int
    cash: float
    capacity: float
    demand: float


def initial_state(rng: np.random.Generator, difficulty: str) -> WorldState:
    return WorldState(week=0, cash=START_CASH, capacity=10.0, demand=float(rng.integers(20, 40)))


def step_world(rng: np.random.Generator, w: WorldState, invest: int) -> float:
    """Advance one week; returns the week's profit."""
    w.capacity += 2 * invest
    sold = min(w.demand, w.capacity)
    profit = sold * PRICE - invest * INVEST_COST
    w.cash += profit
    w.demand = max(0.0, w.demand + float(rng.normal(0, 3)))
    w.week += 1
    return profit
"""[base] Observation → JSON and world registration. Same in every world; do not edit per world."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import gymnasium as gym
import numpy as np

_world: type[gym.Env] | None = None


def register_world(env_cls: type[gym.Env]) -> type[gym.Env]:
    """Register the world's env with Gymnasium (``PlanWorld/<Class>-v0``) and as this server's world."""
    global _world
    _world = env_cls
    env_id = f"PlanWorld/{env_cls.__name__.removesuffix('Env')}-v0"
    if env_id not in gym.registry:
        gym.register(id=env_id, entry_point=env_cls)
    return env_cls


def world() -> type[gym.Env]:
    """The env class registered by ``sim/env.py``."""
    if _world is None:
        import sim.env  # noqa: F401  (registers on import)
    assert _world is not None, "sim/env.py must call register_world(EnvClass)"
    return _world


def to_jsonable(x: Any) -> Any:
    """Recursively turn numpy arrays/scalars (and tuples) into plain JSON values."""
    if isinstance(x, dict):
        return {str(k): to_jsonable(v) for k, v in x.items()}
    if isinstance(x, (list, tuple)):
        return [to_jsonable(v) for v in x]
    if isinstance(x, np.ndarray):
        return to_jsonable(x.tolist())
    if isinstance(x, np.integer):
        return int(x)
    if isinstance(x, np.floating):
        v = float(x)
        return int(v) if v.is_integer() else round(v, 4)
    if isinstance(x, float):
        return int(x) if x.is_integer() else round(x, 4)
    return x


def obs_to_json(obs: dict[str, Any], site_ids: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Dict observation → ``{..., "sites": {id: {key: value}}}``.

    Arrays with one entry per site become per-site fields; everything else
    stays top level (length-1 arrays are unwrapped).
    """
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    sites: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {sid: {} for sid in site_ids}
    for key, value in obs.items():
        arr = np.asarray(value)
        if arr.ndim == 1 and len(arr) == len(site_ids):
            for sid, v in zip(site_ids, arr):
                sites[sid][key] = to_jsonable(v)
        elif arr.ndim == 1 and len(arr) == 1:
            out[key] = to_jsonable(arr[0])
        else:
            out[key] = to_jsonable(value)
    out["sites"] = sites
    return out
# SVG kit

Isometric building blocks for `World.tsx`. Every component returns an SVG `<g>`;
`x, y` is always the screen point where the object stands (its ground centre).
See `src/World.tsx` (Bike Factory) for a full example.

## Rules

- **Painter's order:** draw objects sorted by `i + j` ascending (back to front).
  Ground (island, path/water tiles, rings, flows, moving vehicles) goes first.
- Put the `<svg>` inside `<Stage width height overlay>`; place `Hud` pills in
  `overlay` with `toPercent(x, y, width, height)` so they line up with the SVG.
- Colours are hex strings; faces are shaded automatically.

## iso.ts

- `makeGrid({ cx, cy, n, size, slab = 16 })` → `grid` with `at(i, j)` (tile centre
  on top of the slab), `diamond(i, j, k = 1)` (tile corners, scaled by `k` for
  rings), `uv(i, j)` and the projector `p(u, v, z)`.
- `project(cx, cy)` → `(u, v, z = 0) => [cx + (u − v), cy + (u + v)/2 − z]`.
- `shade(hex, f)` darker for `f < 1`, lighter toward white for `f > 1`.
- `pts(points)` → SVG `points` string. `toPercent(x, y, w, h)` → `{ x, y }` in %.
- `useSvgId(prefix)` → unique id for `<filter>` / `url(#…)`.

## Components

| Component | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Stage` | `width, height, overlay?` | Frame for the SVG + HTML overlay at a fixed aspect ratio. |
| `IsoIsland` | `grid, tileKind?(i, j)` | Floating slab with tiles; kinds `grass`, `path`, `water`, `none`. Children draw on top. |
| `IsoBox` | `x, y, w, d, h, color, top?, z0?, stroke?` | `w` along down-right, `d` along down-left. Left face = color, right 0.8, top 1.3. |
| `Building` | `x, y, w, d, h, color, roof?, gable?, chimney?, windows? = true, z0?` | Windows on both faces; `roof` colour = flat roof box, with `gable` = gable roof. `buildingTop(props)` = drawn height (for Hud placement). |
| `Tree` | `x, y, color?, scale?` | Round crown. |
| `Person` | `x, y, color?, skin?, scale?` | Worker with yellow hard hat. |

# Create worlds with a sandboxed coding agent

**Date:** 2026-10-10
**Status:** proposed

## Context

Decisions 0001, 0003 and 0004 define what a world is. Today the backend only
runs `FakeGenerator`: it copies the template and writes `world.json`. We now
build the real generator: a person enters a name and a description, a coding
agent powered by Gemini Flash writes the world for four difficulty levels, tests
prove it works, and it appears on the website ready to play.

Gaps in the current code that this plan closes:

- The template has 3 difficulties (`easy/medium/hard`); the backend, `/play?level=`
  and the website use 4 levels.
- `FakeLauncher` hands out ports and runs nothing; `/play` proxies plain HTTP to
  port 8000 only, but a world is a server (8000) plus a Vite UI (5173) plus a WebSocket.
- `src/worlds/bike-factory` is the reference world the generator should read, but
  `src/worlds/` is gitignored.
- Demand has no shared building block; every world would reinvent it.

## Decision

### Pipeline

Python in the backend owns the order of steps. The LLM only does the creative
steps. This keeps runs repeatable and lets us show real progress in the existing
SSE stream.

```
POST /worlds ─▶ 1 exists? ─▶ 2 design ─▶ 3 copy template ─▶ 4 fill ─▶ 5 test loop ─▶ 6 smoke ─▶ 7 publish
                  │ yes                     (deterministic)  (agent)   (agent+gates)  (deterministic)
                  └─▶ status "exists", link to the existing world
```

| # | Step | Who | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Exists?** Slug match in the DB and `src/worlds/`, then the agent compares the prompt with titles and premises of all worlds | backend, then agent | Stop with link, or continue |
| 2 | **Design** | agent | `design.md`: storyline, entities, actions, hidden rules, demand model, level table (below) |
| 3 | **Copy template** to `src/worlds/<id>/` and install the locked dependencies | backend | Untouched copy |
| 4 | **Fill** the `[gen]` files from `design.md` | agent | `brief.md`, `secret.md`, `sim/env.py`, `sim/rules.py`, `sim/demand_config.py`, `server/mcp.py`, `ui/src/World.tsx`, `tests/backend/test_rules.py` |
| 5 | **Test loop**: run the gates, feed failures back, at most N rounds | backend runs, agent fixes | Green gates or `failed` |
| 6 | **Smoke boot**: start the world, check `/api/state`, `/mcp` and the UI | backend | Proof it runs for a human |
| 7 | **Publish**: set `path`, `status = ready`, emit `done` | backend | World shows up on the site |

The agent may write only `[gen]` files (allow-list). `[base]` files, including all
`[base]` tests, are checksum-compared with the template before step 5 and 7, so
the agent cannot weaken a gate to turn it green.

### Agent harness: OpenCode with Gemini

- Run OpenCode headless (`opencode run`) as a subprocess in the world folder, with a
  generated `opencode.json`: Gemini provider, model from `PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_GENERATOR_MODEL`,
  file edits limited to the allow-list, bash limited to `pixi run test`, `pixi run tsc`
  and read-only commands.
- Prompts live in `src/backend/.../generator/prompts/` (one per step), each given the
  matching decision docs, `src/worlds-template/README.md`, `ui/src/shared/kit/README.md`
  and the reference world.
- A small parser turns OpenCode's JSON event output into `GenerationEvent`s
  (file written, test run, tool call), so the website shows live progress.
- `Generator` stays a protocol: `OpenCodeGenerator` replaces `FakeGenerator`; the fake
  stays for tests and for running the site without an API key.

**Model name:** "Gemini 3.8 Flash" needs confirming against the Gemini API model list
when the key exists. The model is an env var, not hard-coded.

**Fallback:** if OpenCode is flaky for streaming or permissions, write a ~200-line
PydanticAI loop with tools `read`, `write` (allow-listed), `run_tests`. Decision 0001
already uses PydanticAI + Gemini for the playing agent, so it is a known quantity.
Decide after the spike in phase 1.

### Four difficulty levels

Levels are **cumulative**, fixed by one table in `sim/env.py`, so rules are written once:

| Level | Name | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Starter | Core loop, 1–2 sites, 3–4 actions, no hidden rules, no noise |
| 2 | Standard | More sites, one hidden rule, a lead time or capacity limit |
| 3 | Hard | Competitor or event instances, weather, 2–3 hidden rules, fog, action budget |
| 4 | Expert | All demand factors, delayed effects, interacting hidden rules, noise on |

Template changes: `DIFFICULTIES` becomes `("level1".."level4")` with display names
`Starter … Expert`; `test_env.py` loops over four; `ui_state` returns `difficulty` as
level number and name; `POST /api/reset` takes `level`. Level 4 is meant to be like the
FoodTruckBench expert mode: many interacting hidden factors, and the agent sees only
the resulting sales and demand signals, never the formula.

### Demand component

New `[base]` module `sim/demand.py` that every world uses, following the multiplicative
model in the screenshot:

```
demand = base × price × location × weather × time × day_of_week × events
              × variety × competition × reputation × popularity × noise
```

- A `DemandModel` is a list of `Factor`s, each `(site, state, rng) -> float` with a
  neutral value of 1.0. The module ships ready factors: `price_elasticity`, `affinity`
  (site × audience), `weather`, `seasonality` (time and day of week), `events`, `variety`,
  `competition`, `reputation` (log of reviews), `popularity` (grows with fulfilment),
  `noise`.
- The generator does not write formulas. It writes `sim/demand_config.py`: which factors
  exist, their parameters (drawn from the seed) and which levels enable them.
- `env.py` calls `demand.compute(site)` and exposes only sales and unmet demand.
- `secret.md` lists active factors (generated from the config) for reviewers.
- **UI:** `Discoveries` shows a factor as "found" once the agent or the human has probed
  it, so the demand model is visible in the world without leaking early. This is my
  reading of "somewhere in this world"; tell me if you meant something else.

### Tests and gates (sandbox)

All run with `pixi run test` and `pixi run test-ui` inside the sandbox. Existing `[base]`
tests stay; new generic `[base]` tests are added:

| Gate | Checks |
|---|---|
| `check_env` + determinism | Per level, same seed and actions give the same trace |
| Contract | `check_action`, `encode_actions`, `ui_state` shape equals `mockState` |
| MCP / API | Every verb in `env.actions` is a tool and a route; WebSocket events work |
| **Playability** (new) | Baseline policy scores strictly between 0 and 1 on every level; a do-nothing policy scores less than baseline; baseline score does not increase with level |
| **No leak** (new) | Strings from `secret.md` and factor parameters do not appear in `brief`, `observe` or `/api/state` |
| **Demand** (new) | Factors are 1.0 when disabled; demand is non-negative and finite over a seeded rollout |
| Frontend | `tsc`, `vite build`, Vitest render of `World.tsx` with `mockState` |
| Smoke | Boot, `GET /api/state`, MCP `list_tools`, UI HTML 200 |
| `test_run.py` | Optional: one Gemini agent run at level 1 (a later phase) |

Sandbox: phase 1 is a subprocess in a worker container with a temp world dir, wall-clock
and round limits, and an egress allow-list (Gemini API only; dependencies pre-installed
from the template's lock files, so no registry access is needed). Phase 3 hardens this to
one container per generation. Prompts come from the public site, so treat generated code
as untrusted.

### Going live

- **Real launcher:** `ProcessLauncher` runs `pixi run serve` for the world on a free port
  and tracks the process; the reaper (already present) stops idle worlds.
- **One port per world:** the template builds the UI (`vite build`) and serves it from
  `server/api.py` at `/`, with a relative base path. `/play/<id>/` then proxies one origin.
  The dev setup (Vite on 5173) stays for `pixi run dev`.
- **WebSocket:** `/play` currently proxies plain HTTP only. Add an SSE variant of
  `/api/events` and use that in the UI (simplest), or proxy the WebSocket.
- **Website:** new generation steps and the `exists` status in `PromptWindow` and
  `WorldDetail`; the catalogue already lists `ready` worlds and the level picker
  already links `/play/<id>/?level=N`. On `ready`, the card gets a Play button without
  a reload because the SSE `done` event already exists.
- **Human first, agent later:** both use the same `Game`, so no extra work for humans;
  the agent harness only needs the world's `/mcp` URL.

## Phases

| Phase | Scope | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Branch, API key, move the reference world to a committed `src/worlds-reference/` | Agent can read it |
| 1 | Template to 4 levels; `demand.py`; new gates; **spike** OpenCode vs PydanticAI on one hand-written prompt | `pixi run test` is green on the template at all levels |
| 2 | `OpenCodeGenerator`, steps 1–7, event streaming, allow-list and checksum guard | One prompt produces a world that passes the gates |
| 3 | `ProcessLauncher`, single-port UI, SSE events, website step updates | A new world is playable by a human from the site |
| 4 | Hardening: container per run, retries and cost caps, `test_run.py`, agent-vs-you play | Public use is safe |

Cut line for the demo: phases 0–3.

## Consequences

- Most of the quality comes from the template, `demand.py` and the gates, not from the
  prompt; a world is only "live" if the gates are green.
- Step order is code, so the agent cannot skip checks, and we can retry single steps.
- Template changes (4 levels, single-port UI) do not reach worlds generated earlier.
- The agent writes less code per world, because levels are a table and demand is a
  config, which fits a Flash-class model.

## Alternatives considered

- **Let the agent run the whole workflow from one prompt:** rejected; it can skip the
  exists check, edit tests, or declare success without running anything.
- **One generation per level:** rejected; four separate rule sets drift apart and cost
  four times as much.
- **Generate demand formulas freely:** rejected; unbounded formulas break the playability
  gates and are hard to review.
- **Claude Code as the generator (decision 0001 option):** rejected here; the goal is
  Gemini Flash for cost and speed.

## Open questions

- Exact Gemini model ID and quota for parallel generations (`max_generating` is 3).
- Whether OpenCode's JSON events are rich enough for live progress (decided in the spike).
- Time and token budget per world before we mark it `failed`.

## Supersedes

None

# Create worlds with a sandboxed coding agent

**Date:** 2026-10-10
**Status:** proposed

## Context

Decisions 0001, 0003 and 0004 define what a world is. Today the backend only
runs `FakeGenerator` (copies the template, writes `world.json`) and `FakeLauncher`
(hands out ports, runs nothing). We now build the real thing: a person enters a
name and a description, a coding agent powered by Gemini Flash writes the world
for **three difficulty levels**, tests prove it works, and it appears on the
website ready to play.

Gaps in the current code that this plan closes:

- The website, `generator.py`, `/play` and their tests say four levels; the
  template already has three (`easy`, `medium`, `hard`). **Three wins.**
- `/play` proxies plain HTTP to one port; a world is a server (8000) plus a Vite
  UI (5173) plus a WebSocket, and its UI uses absolute `/api/...` URLs.
- `pixi run` would install a full conda environment per world; far too slow on
  first play.
- `src/worlds/bike-factory` is the reference world for the agent, but
  `src/worlds/` is gitignored.
- Demand has no shared building block.
- A world server holds one shared `Game`; two public visitors would fight over it.

## Decision

### Pipeline

Python in the backend owns the order of steps; the LLM does only the creative
ones. Runs are repeatable and each step is a real progress event.

```
POST /worlds ─▶ 1 exists? ─▶ 2 design ─▶ 3 copy ─▶ 4 fill ─▶ 5 test loop ─▶ 6 build+smoke ─▶ 7 publish
                  │ yes                   backend   agent    backend runs,     backend          backend
                  └─▶ status "exists"                        agent fixes
```

| # | Step key | Who | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `check_exists` | backend: slug match in DB and on disk. Then one Gemini call with structured output compares the prompt with all titles and premises: `{exists: bool, world_id}` | continue, or status `exists` + `duplicate_of` |
| 2 | `design` | agent | `design.md`: storyline, entities, actions, hidden rules, demand factors, level table |
| 3 | `copy_template` | backend | `src/worlds/<id>/` from the template; `[base]` checksums stored |
| 4 | `fill` | agent | `brief.md`, `secret.md`, `sim/env.py`, `sim/rules.py`, `sim/demand_config.py`, `server/mcp.py`, `ui/src/World.tsx`, `tests/backend/test_rules.py` |
| 5 | `tests` | backend runs the gates; agent fixes failures, max `N` rounds | green gates or `failed` |
| 6 | `smoke` | backend: build the UI, boot the world, hit `/api/state`, MCP `list_tools` and `/` | proof it runs |
| 7 | `publish` | backend | write `world.json` and `thumbnail.png`, set `path`, `status = ready` |

The agent may only write the `[gen]` files above (allow-list in OpenCode's
permission config). Before steps 5 and 7 the backend compares `[base]` file
checksums with the template, so the agent cannot weaken a test to turn it green.

### Agent loop: OpenCode is the loop; no PydanticAI wrapper

OpenCode already is a coding-agent loop (read, edit, bash, retries, context
management) and supports Gemini. Wrapping it in PydanticAI would give two loops
and no benefit. PydanticAI stays where decision 0001 put it: the **playing**
agent, which is a different job.

How the backend uses OpenCode:

1. For each generation, spawn `opencode serve --port <free>` with the world
   folder as working directory and the Gemini key in its environment. A
   generated `opencode.json` in the world folder sets the provider, the model
   (`PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_GENERATOR_MODEL`), the `world-builder` agent prompt and
   permissions: edit only allow-listed paths, bash only `pixi run test*`,
   `pixi run tsc` and read-only commands.
2. Talk to it over its HTTP API with `httpx` (create session, send prompt, read
   the event stream). This is what the OpenCode SDK wraps; the official SDK is
   TypeScript, so a Python backend calling the API directly avoids a Node
   sidecar. Fallback if the API is awkward: a ~50-line Node script using
   `@opencode-ai/sdk` that prints JSON lines for the backend to read.
3. **One OpenCode session per world.** Prompts go in order: `design`, `fill`,
   then one `fix` prompt per failed test round containing the failing output.
   The session keeps context between them. The session id is stored so a retry
   can resume.
4. Map OpenCode events (file written, tool call, bash result) to
   `GenerationEvent`s. That is the live detail in the website's progress list.
5. Stop the server when the run ends; enforce a wall-clock timeout and a token
   cap.

Step 1 does not need a loop: one structured Gemini call (plain `google-genai`
with a JSON schema; PydanticAI is fine here if it is already a dependency).

A spike in Step A below validates that the HTTP API and event stream behave as
described before we build on them. I have not run OpenCode yet.

### Three difficulty levels

Levels are cumulative and driven by one table in `sim/env.py`, so the rules are
written once. Level N maps to `DIFFICULTIES[N-1]`.

| Level | Name | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Easy | Core loop, 1–2 sites, 3–4 actions, no hidden rules, noise off |
| 2 | Medium | More sites, 1–2 hidden rules, lead times or capacity limits, weather |
| 3 | Hard | The expert mode: competitors and events, all demand factors, 3+ interacting hidden rules, fog, action budget, noise on. The agent sees sales and demand signals, never the formula |

### Demand component

New `[base]` module `sim/demand.py`, used by every world, following the
multiplicative model in the FoodTruckBench screenshot:

```
demand = base × price × location × weather × time × day_of_week × events
              × variety × competition × reputation × popularity × noise
```

- A `DemandModel` is a list of `Factor`s `(site, state, rng) -> float`, neutral
  value 1.0. Shipped factors: `price_elasticity`, `affinity`, `weather`,
  `seasonality` (time, day of week), `events`, `variety`, `competition`,
  `reputation` (log of reviews), `popularity`, `noise`.
- The generator writes **no formulas**, only `sim/demand_config.py`: which
  factors exist, their parameters (drawn from the seed) and the first level that
  enables each.
- `env.py` calls `demand.compute(site)` and exposes only sales and unmet demand.
- `Discoveries` marks a factor as found once it has been probed. My reading of
  "somewhere in this world"; correct me if you meant a visible panel or chart.

### Gates (the sandbox)

`pixi run test` and `pixi run test-ui` inside the sandbox. Existing `[base]`
tests stay; new `[base]` tests are marked **new**.

| Gate | Checks |
|---|---|
| `test_env.py` | `check_env` and determinism per level |
| contract | `check_action`, `encode_actions`, `ui_state` shape equals `mockState` |
| `test_mcp.py`, `test_api.py` | every verb is a tool and a route; events work |
| `test_playability.py` **new** | baseline scores in (0, 1) on every level; do-nothing < baseline; baseline never improves with level |
| `test_no_leak.py` **new** | words from `secret.md` and factor parameters never appear in `brief`, `observe` or `/api/state` |
| `test_demand.py` **new** | disabled factors are 1.0; demand finite and ≥ 0 over a seeded rollout |
| frontend | `tsc`, `vite build`, Vitest render of `World.tsx` with `mockState` |
| smoke | boot, `/api/state`, MCP `list_tools`, `/` returns HTML |
| `test_run.py` | optional: one Gemini agent run at level 1 (later) |

The sandbox is a subprocess in the API container with its own temp directory,
no secrets except the Gemini key, wall-clock and round limits. Dependencies come
from a prebuilt shared environment, so tests need no network. Prompts come from a
public site, so generated code is untrusted; container-per-run is a later
hardening step.

### Routing and going live: nothing is configured per world

Routing is data-driven. A world is one row in the database plus one folder on
disk:

```
Browser ─▶ nginx ─ /api/play/<id>/?level=2 ─▶ API  GET /play/<id>/
                                                │ 1. look up the row (id → status, path, port)
                                                │ 2. not running? launcher starts it, waits for /healthz
                                                │ 3. proxy to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/
                                                ▼
                                          world server (FastAPI: /api, /mcp, built UI at /)
```

- `/worlds/:id` in the website is one generic React route; the catalogue is
  `GET /worlds`. Publishing a world means setting `status = ready` and `path`.
  No route, nginx or frontend change is needed.
- **`ProcessLauncher`** runs `<shared-env>/bin/python -m uvicorn server.api:app --port N`
  with the world folder as working directory. Dependencies are `[base]` and fixed,
  so one environment baked into the API image serves every world; nothing is
  installed per world. It picks a free port, waits for `/healthz`, tracks the PID;
  the existing reaper stops idle worlds.
- **UI served by the world server:** step 6 builds the UI (`vite build`, using a
  shared `node_modules` symlinked in). `server/api.py` serves `ui/dist` at `/`.
  Vite `base: "./"` and `api.ts` use relative URLs (`api/state`), so the UI works
  behind the `/api/play/<id>/` prefix.
- **Events:** the proxy is plain HTTP, so the UI uses SSE for `/api/events` (the
  WebSocket stays for direct use).
- **Level:** `?level=N` is forwarded; the world UI reads it on load and calls
  `POST /api/reset {level}`.
- **Visitors:** the world server keeps one `Game` per player cookie (capped, LRU)
  instead of one global `Game`. The agent connects to `/mcp?player=<id>`. Demo
  shortcut if time is short: one shared `Game`, reset when a level is opened.

### How a world is stored and shown

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `worlds` table (SQLite) | Metadata only: `id`, `title`, `prompt`, `seed`, `status` (`queued`, `generating`, `ready`, `failed`, **`exists`**), `storyline`, `path`, `running`, `port`, `featured`, `play_count`, `creator_hash` |
| new columns (migration `0004`) | `duplicate_of`, `agent_session_id`, `model`, `gen_seconds`, `gate_report` (JSON of the last test run) |
| `world_events` table | One row per progress event, streamed to the website over SSE |
| `src/worlds/<id>/` (volume) | The world itself: code, `world.json`, `thumbnail.png`. Source of truth for the game |

The main website never renders a world. It shows the catalogue card (title,
premise, thumbnail, status, play count), the generation progress, and three
**Play at Easy / Medium / Hard** links. The link opens the world's own UI in a
new tab. This matches decision 0001: no shared frontend that must integrate every
generated world. `thumbnail.png` is a Playwright screenshot of level 1, served
by `GET /worlds/<id>/thumbnail`; featured worlds keep their static images.

## Implementation steps

Sizes are rough: S under an hour, M a few hours, L most of a day.

**A. Spike (S).** Install OpenCode locally with the Gemini key. Verify: provider
config, `opencode serve` HTTP API, event stream, permissions, one prompt that
edits `brief.md` in a copy of the template. Decide go or fallback (PydanticAI
loop with tools `read`, `write`, `run_tests`). *Done when:* I can drive one
session from a Python script and print its events.

**B. Template to three levels and level in the URL (M).** Files in
`src/worlds-template/`:
- `sim/helpers.py`: add `LEVELS = {1: "easy", 2: "medium", 3: "hard"}`.
- `server/api.py`: `reset` accepts `level`; per-player `Game` registry; serve
  `ui/dist`; add `/healthz`; SSE variant of `/api/events`.
- `ui/`: `vite.config.ts` base `./`; `api.ts` relative URLs and SSE; `App.tsx`
  reads `?level=`; `Brand` shows "Easy / Medium / Hard".
- `pixi.toml`: tasks `build-ui`, `test-ui`.
- Tests: reset by level, static UI served, two cookies get two games.

**C. Demand module and new gates (M).** `sim/demand.py`, `sim/demand_config.py`
placeholder, `tests/backend/test_demand.py`, `test_playability.py`,
`test_no_leak.py`; make the placeholder world use the demand model so the gates
run green on the template. Show found factors in `Discoveries`.

**D. Reference world (S).** Copy `src/worlds/bike-factory` to a committed
`src/worlds-reference/bike-factory` and bring it to the new contract (three
levels, demand config). The agent reads it as the example. Point
`worlds-template/README.md` at the new path.

**E. Website: three levels (S).** `src/web/src/`:
- `components/DifficultySection.tsx`: `LEVELS = ["Easy", "Medium", "Hard"]`,
  heading "Three levels in every world", copy "all three", and three cells per
  table row.
- `components/PromptWindow.tsx:72`, `components/ExistingWorlds.tsx:101`,
  `pages/WorldDetail.tsx`: "four" becomes "three".
- `components/PlayLevels.tsx`: show `Easy / Medium / Hard` labels with the level
  number in the `aria-label`.
- Tests: `DifficultySection.test.tsx`, `Home.test.tsx`, `ExistingWorlds.test.tsx`
  (`levels: [1, 2, 3]`, three links).
- Backend: `generator.py` `LEVELS = (1, 2, 3)`; `api/play.py` `le=3`;
  `tests/test_worlds_api.py` expects `[1, 2, 3]`. No migration, levels are not
  stored.

**F. Generator package (L).** Replace `generator.py` with a package:

```
generator/__init__.py          Generator protocol, GenerationRequest, GenerationEvent
generator/fake.py              FakeGenerator (kept for tests and key-less runs)
generator/opencode_generator.py  runs steps 1–7 in order
generator/opencode_client.py   spawn `opencode serve`, session, prompt, event stream
generator/exists.py            step 1
generator/gates.py             run pixi tests, parse the report, checksum guard
generator/prompts/             design.md, fill.md, fix.md, exists.md
generator/opencode_template/   opencode.json, world-builder agent prompt
```

Settings in `config.py`: `generator` (`fake` or `opencode`), `gemini_api_key`,
`generator_model`, `fix_rounds`, `generator_timeout_seconds`. `main.py` picks the
generator from settings. Tests: step ordering with a stubbed client, the checksum
guard catches an edited `[base]` file, failed gates end in `failed` with the
report in `gate_report`.

**G. Database and runner (S).** Migration `0004` with the new columns. `runner.py`
handles the `exists` outcome and stores `agent_session_id` and `gate_report`.
`retry` resumes the session. `POST /worlds` answers 409 with the world id for an
exact slug match.

**H. Launcher and play route (M).** `launcher.py`: `ProcessLauncher`
(free port, spawn, `/healthz` wait, stop); `play.py` returns a "starting" page
that retries instead of the placeholder when the world is slow to boot. Tests
with a tiny stub server.

**I. Website generation progress (S).** `WorldDetail.tsx` `STEPS` becomes
`check_exists`, `design`, `copy_template`, `fill`, `tests`, `smoke`, `publish`,
with a per-file and per-test-round detail line; an "already exists" card with a
link to `duplicate_of`; `StatusChip` handles `exists`; catalogue card shows the
thumbnail. Update `PromptWindow` copy.

**J. Deployment (S).** API image gets Node, `opencode`, the shared Python and
`node_modules` environment, Chromium for thumbnails; `compose.yaml` passes
`GEMINI_API_KEY` and the generator settings; `.env.example` documents them;
README gets a section.

**K. End to end (M).** Generate three different prompts, fix the template and
prompts where the agent gets stuck, record time and tokens per world. *Done
when:* a new world appears on the site, passes all gates and plays at all three
levels in a browser.

**L. Hardening (L, after the demo).** Container per generation with an egress
allow-list, per-visitor cost caps, `test_run.py` with the Gemini player, agent
vs. you in the same world.

Order: A first; B, C, D, E in parallel (different files); then F, G, H, I; then
J and K. Cut line for the demo: A–K.

## Consequences

- Quality comes from the template, `demand.py` and the gates more than from the
  prompt; a world is live only if the gates are green.
- Step order is code, so the agent cannot skip checks and single steps can be
  retried.
- The agent writes less per world, since levels are a table and demand is a
  config, which fits a Flash-class model.
- Template changes (levels in the URL, single port, per-player games) do not
  reach worlds generated earlier.

## Alternatives considered

- **PydanticAI loop around Gemini instead of OpenCode:** more code to own
  (tools, edit format, retries); kept as the fallback.
- **OpenCode wrapped in PydanticAI:** two loops for one job.
- **Agent runs the whole workflow from one prompt:** it can skip the exists
  check, edit tests, or claim success without running anything.
- **One generation per level:** three rule sets drift apart and cost three times
  as much.
- **Free-form demand formulas:** break the playability gates and are hard to
  review.
- **`pixi install` per world:** minutes on first play.
- **Store worlds in the database:** code is a folder tree that tests and servers
  need on disk.

## Open questions

- Exact Gemini model ID, quota and cost per world.
- Whether OpenCode's event stream is detailed enough (decided by the spike).
- Time and token budget per world before it counts as `failed`.
- Per-player `Game` or the shared-game shortcut for the first demo.

## Supersedes

class Game:
    """One running world: env, this step's queued actions, event log, discoveries."""

    # UI controls handled here, not by the env: id → steps to advance.
    ADVANCE_CONTROLS = {"play": 1, "fast": 4}
    NOOP_CONTROLS = {"pause", "stats"}

    def __init__(self, seed: int | None = None, difficulty: str | None = None):
        self.env_cls: Any = world()
        self.events: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.scores: list[float] = []  # final scores of earlier episodes
        self.mode = "you"
        self._seq = 0
        self._lock = threading.RLock()
        self._subs: set[tuple[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, asyncio.Queue]] = set()
        self.reset(seed, difficulty, source="system")

    # ---------- actions ----------

    def reset(self, seed: int | None = None, difficulty: str | None = None, source: str = "ui") -> dict[str, Any]:
        with self._lock:
            difficulty = difficulty or getattr(self, "difficulty", None) or "medium"
            if difficulty not in self.env_cls.DIFFICULTIES:
                raise ValueError(f"difficulty must be one of {self.env_cls.DIFFICULTIES}")
            if getattr(self, "env", None) is not None and self.env.score()["week"] > 1:
                self.scores.append(self.env.score()["score"])
            self.seed = int(seed) if seed is not None else 1000 + secrets.randbelow(9000)
            self.difficulty = difficulty
            self.env = self.env_cls(difficulty)
            self.env.reset(seed=self.seed)
            self.queued: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []
            self.discoveries: list[str] = []
            self.notes: list[str] = []
            self.story: dict[str, Any] | None = None
            self.active: str | None = None
            self.baseline = self._baseline_score()
            result = {"seed": self.seed, "difficulty": difficulty}
            self._log(source, "reset", "reset", {"seed": seed, "difficulty": difficulty}, result)
            return result

    def act(self, verb: str, args: dict[str, Any] | None = None, source: str = "ui") -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Queue a world action for this step, or run a UI control (play, fast, new_world, mode…)."""
        args = dict(args or {})
        with self._lock:
            if verb in self.ADVANCE_CONTROLS:
                return self.advance(self.ADVANCE_CONTROLS[verb], source)
            if verb in self.NOOP_CONTROLS:
                return {"ok": True}
            if verb == "new_world":
                return self.reset(None, self.difficulty, source)
            if verb == "mode":
                if args.get("mode") not in ("you", "agent"):
                    raise ValueError("mode must be 'you' or 'agent'")
                self.mode = args["mode"]

content.text:
I updated the plan in `docs/design-decisions/0005-create-worlds-with-a-sandboxed-coding-agent.md`. It's uncommitted, and I haven't run any of it.

**Template changes**
- The plan now has a full table of template changes. The main ones:
  - **Levels:** a `LEVELS` map (1/2/3 → easy/medium/hard) and `reset` by level.
  - **Players:** `server/api.py` gets a registry of games, one per player, instead of one global game.
  - **MCP:** `/mcp` becomes a small dispatcher that builds one MCP app per player, so the generated `server/mcp.py` contract doesn't change.
  - **UI and serving:** a `/healthz` route, the built UI served from the world server, SSE events, and a UI that uses relative URLs and reads `?level=`.
  - **Demand:** the new `sim/demand.py` and `sim/demand_config.py`.
  - **Gates:** new playability, no-leak and demand tests.
- The template has no frontend tests yet, although decision 0003 lists them. So the plan adds Vitest and a render test.

**Time and cost budget**
- Since tokens are free today, wall-clock time is the cost that matters.
- My target is about 10 minutes per world, with a hard cap of 15 minutes and then `failed`.
- The caps are 4 test-fix rounds, 2 polish rounds, 1.5M input tokens and 150k output tokens per world, as a guard against runaway loops.
- These numbers are estimates until the end-to-end step measures them. I don't know Gemini's pricing for the model you picked.
- To get a very nice looking world, I added a `polish` step. It screenshots each level, has Gemini critique the screenshots against a visual checklist, and fixes `World.tsx`.
- To keep worlds fast, the design prompt limits a world to at most 4 sites and 5 actions. Writing the simulator and the UI in parallel could later save about 2 minutes.
- For the demo, pre-generate two or three worlds and generate one live.

**Shared game**
- There's no load balancer, and you don't need one locally. The chain already exists: nginx forwards to the API, and the API's `/play` route is an `httpx` proxy that knows each world's port from the database.
- I'd run one process per world with one game per player. The world UI makes a random player id and sends it as `?player=<id>` on every request, including SSE. The proxy already forwards query strings, so it needs no change.
- The agent can later connect to `/mcp?player=<id>`, either to its own game or to the human's for "agent vs you".
- I dropped the shared-game shortcut, because the per-player registry is small.
- If this is ever hosted, the API's proxy is the part to swap out, and the world servers stay as they are.

Can you hard cap the time at 5mins per world please?
- We develop everything locally and also just play it locally. The scenario where 2 players play the same world should not happen

  keeps a registry `player_id → Game` (LRU, max 50, idle games dropped after 30
  minutes). The player id is a random id the world UI creates in `sessionStorage`
  and sends as `?player=<id>` on every request (query parameter, so SSE works too).

  `httpx` reverse proxy) → world server, and the API already knows each world's
  port from the database. A missing id uses a `default` game, so `curl` and tests
  still work.
- **Agent later:** it connects to `/mcp?player=<id>`, so it can play its own game
  next to a human, or the same game as the human ("agent vs you" with the same
  seed).

  replace (for example nginx with `X-Accel-Redirect` to the world's port), and the
  world servers stay unchanged.

### How a world is stored and shown

| Where | What |
|---|---|
prompts where the agent gets stuck, record time and tokens per world and set the caps from the budget table. *Done
when:* a new world appears on the site, passes all gates and plays at all three
levels in a browser.

**L. Hardening (L, after the demo).** Container per generation with an egress
allow-list, per-visitor cost caps, `test_run.py` with the Gemini player, agent
vs. you in the same world.

- Step order is code, so the agent cannot skip checks and single steps can be
  retried.
- The agent writes less per world, since levels are a table and demand is a
  config, which fits a Flash-class model.
- Template changes (levels in the URL, single port, per-player games) do not
  reach worlds generated earlier.

## Alternatives considered

- **PydanticAI loop around Gemini instead of OpenCode:** more code to own
  (tools, edit format, retries); kept as the fallback.
- **OpenCode wrapped in PydanticAI:** two loops for one job.
- **Agent runs the whole workflow from one prompt:** it can skip the exists
  check, edit tests, or claim success without running anything.
- **One generation per level:** three rule sets drift apart and cost three times
  as much.
- **Free-form demand formulas:** break the playability gates and are hard to
  review.
- **`pixi install` per world:** minutes on first play.
- **Store worlds in the database:** code is a folder tree that tests and servers
  need on disk.

## Open questions

- Exact Gemini model ID and price (tokens are free today).
- Whether OpenCode's event stream is detailed enough (decided by the spike).

28	
29	### Pipeline
30	
31	Python in the backend owns the order of steps; the LLM does only the creative
32	ones. Runs are repeatable and each step is a real progress event.
33	
34	```
35	POST /worlds ─▶ 1 exists? ─▶ 2 design ─▶ 3 copy ─▶ 4 fill ─▶ 5 tests ─▶ 6 polish ─▶ 7 smoke ─▶ 8 publish
36	                  │ yes                   backend   agent    runs gates,  looks at     backend    backend
37	                  └─▶ status "exists"                        agent fixes  screenshots
38	```
39	
40	| # | Step key | Who | Output |
41	|---|---|---|---|
42	| 1 | `check_exists` | backend: slug match in DB and on disk. Then one Gemini call with structured output compares the prompt with all titles and premises: `{exists: bool, world_id}` | continue, or status `exists` + `duplicate_of` |
43	| 2 | `design` | agent | `design.md`: storyline, entities, actions, hidden rules, demand factors, level table, the `ui_state` shape (so sim and UI can be written independently), a visual concept (palette, layout of the island) |

45	| 4 | `fill` | agent | `brief.md`, `secret.md`, `sim/env.py`, `sim/rules.py`, `sim/demand_config.py`, `server/mcp.py`, `ui/src/World.tsx`, `tests/backend/test_rules.py` |
46	| 5 | `tests` | backend runs the gates; agent fixes failures, max `N` rounds | green gates or `failed` |

49	| 8 | `publish` | backend | write `world.json` and `thumbnail.png`, set `path`, `status = ready` |
50

52	permission config). Before `tests` and `publish` the backend compares `[base]` file
53	checksums with the template, so the agent cannot weaken a test to turn it green.
54	
55	### Agent loop: OpenCode is the loop; no PydanticAI wrapper

57	OpenCode already is a coding-agent loop (read, edit, bash, retries, context
58	management) and supports Gemini. Wrapping it in PydanticAI would give two loops
59	and no benefit. PydanticAI stays where decision 0001 put it: the **playing**
60	agent, which is a different job.

65	   folder as working directory and the Gemini key in its environment. A
66	   generated `opencode.json` in the world folder sets the provider, the model

206	order: `polish`, then the number of kit objects asked for, then the world size.
207	
208	For the demo, pre-generate two or three worlds and keep live generation for one
209	prompt; four minutes of visible progress is watchable.
210	
211	### Routing and going live: nothing is configured per world
212	
213	Routing is data-driven. A world is one row in the database plus one folder on
214	disk:
215	
216	```
217	Browser ─▶ nginx ─ /api/play/<id>/?level=2 ─▶ API  GET /play/<id>/
218	                                                │ 1. look up the row (id → status, path, port)
219	                                                │ 2. not running? launcher starts it, waits for /healthz
220	                                                │ 3. proxy to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/
221	                                                ▼
222	                                          world server (FastAPI: /api, /mcp, built UI at /)
223	```
224	
225	- `/worlds/:id` in the website is one generic React route; the catalogue is
226	  `GET /worlds`. Publishing a world means setting `status = ready` and `path`.
227	  No route, nginx or frontend change is needed.
228	- **`ProcessLauncher`** runs `<shared-env>/bin/python -m uvicorn server.api:app --port N`
229	  with the world folder as working directory. Dependencies are `[base]` and fixed,
230	  so one environment baked into the API image serves every world; nothing is
231	  installed per world. It picks a free port, waits for `/healthz`, tracks the PID;
232	  the existing reaper stops idle worlds.
233	- **UI served by the world server:** the `smoke` step builds the UI (`vite build`, using a
234	  shared `node_modules` symlinked in). `server/api.py` serves `ui/dist` at `/`.
235	  Vite `base: "./"` and `api.ts` use relative URLs (`api/state`), so the UI works
236	  behind the `/api/play/<id>/` prefix.
237	- **Events:** the proxy is plain HTTP, so the UI uses SSE for `/api/events` (the
238	  WebSocket stays for direct use).
239	- **Level:** `?level=N` is forwarded; the world UI reads it on load and calls
240	  `POST /api/reset {level}`.
241	- **One game per world server:** the shared `Game` in `server/api.py` is kept. Only
242	  one player uses a world at a time on your machine, so there is no player id, no
243	  per-player registry and nothing to add to the proxy. The chain stays nginx → API
244	  (`/play`, an `httpx` reverse proxy) → world server; the API already knows each
245	  world's port from the database. There is no load balancer and none is needed.
246	- **Agent later:** it connects to the world's existing `/mcp` and plays the same
247	  `Game` as the UI, which is how the "You / Agent" toggle in decision 0004 works.
248	- If this is ever hosted for many visitors, the first change is a game per player
249	  in the world server; it is deliberately left out now.
250	
251	### How a world is stored and shown
252	
253	| Where | What |
254	|---|---|
255	| `worlds` table (SQLite) | Metadata only: `id`, `title`, `prompt`, `seed`, `status` (`queued`, `generating`, `ready`, `failed`, **`exists`**), `storyline`, `path`, `running`, `port`, `featured`, `play_count`, `creator_hash` |
256	| new columns (migration `0004`) | `duplicate_of`, `agent_sessions`, `model`, `gen_seconds`, `gate_report` (JSON of the last test run) |
257	| `world_events` table | One row per progress event, streamed to the website over SSE |
258	| `src/worlds/<id>/` (volume) | The world itself: code, `world.json`, `thumbnail.png`. Source of truth for the game |
259	
260	The main website never renders a world. It shows the catalogue card (title,
261	premise, thumbnail, status, play count), the generation progress, and three
262	**Play at Easy / Medium / Hard** links. The link opens the world's own UI in a
263	new tab. This matches decision 0001: no shared frontend that must integrate every
264	generated world. `thumbnail.png` is a Playwright screenshot of level 1, served
265	by `GET /worlds/<id>/thumbnail`; featured worlds keep their static images.
266	
267	## Implementation steps
268	
269	Sizes are rough: S under an hour, M a few hours, L most of a day.
270	
271	**A. Spike (S).** Install OpenCode locally with the Gemini key. Verify: provider
272	config, `opencode serve` HTTP API, event stream, permissions, one prompt that
273	edits `brief.md` in a copy of the template. Decide go or fallback (PydanticAI
274	loop with tools `read`, `write`, `run_tests`). *Done when:* I can drive one
275	session from a Python script and print its events.
276	
277	**B. Template: levels, one port, tests (M).** Everything in the table
278	"Template changes" except the demand files, in this order: `LEVELS` and `reset`
279	by level → `/healthz` and static UI → SSE → UI changes → tests. *Done when:*
280	`pixi run test` passes and the built UI works when opened through
281	`/api/play/<id>/?level=2`.
282	
283	**C. Demand module, new gates and Vitest (M).** `sim/demand.py`, `sim/demand_config.py`
284	placeholder, `tests/backend/test_demand.py`, `test_playability.py`,
285	`test_no_leak.py`, and the frontend test setup; make the placeholder world use the demand model so the gates
286	run green on the template. Show found factors in `Discoveries`.
287	
288	**D. Reference world (S).** Copy `src/worlds/bike-factory` to a committed
289	`src/worlds-reference/bike-factory` and bring it to the new contract (three
290	levels, demand config). The agent reads it as the example. Point
291	`worlds-template/README.md` at the new path.
292	
293	**E. Website: three levels (S).** `src/web/src/`:
294	- `components/DifficultySection.tsx`: `LEVELS = ["Easy", "Medium", "Hard"]`,
295	  heading "Three levels in every world", copy "all three", and three cells per
296	  table row.
297	- `components/PromptWindow.tsx:72`, `components/ExistingWorlds.tsx:101`,
298	  `pages/WorldDetail.tsx`: "four" becomes "three".
299	- `components/PlayLevels.tsx`: show `Easy / Medium / Hard` labels with the level
300	  number in the `aria-label`.
301	- Tests: `DifficultySection.test.tsx`, `Home.test.tsx`, `ExistingWorlds.test.tsx`
302	  (`levels: [1, 2, 3]`, three links).
303	- Backend: `generator.py` `LEVELS = (1, 2, 3)`; `api/play.py` `le=3`;
304	  `tests/test_worlds_api.py` expects `[1, 2, 3]`. No migration, levels are not
305	  stored.
306	
307	**F. Generator package (L).** Replace `generator.py` with a package:
308	
309	```
310	generator/__init__.py          Generator protocol, GenerationRequest, GenerationEvent
311	generator/fake.py              FakeGenerator (kept for tests and key-less runs)
312	generator/opencode_generator.py  runs steps 1–8 in order
313	generator/opencode_client.py   spawn `opencode serve`, session, prompt, event stream
314	generator/exists.py            step 1
315	generator/gates.py             run pixi tests, parse the report, checksum guard
316	generator/prompts/             design.md, fill.md, fix.md, exists.md
317	generator/opencode_template/   opencode.json, world-builder agent prompt
318	```
319	
320	Settings in `config.py`: `generator` (`fake` or `opencode`), `gemini_api_key`,
321	`generator_model`, `fix_rounds`, `generator_timeout_seconds`. `main.py` picks the
322	generator from settings. Tests: step ordering with a stubbed client, the checksum
323	guard catches an edited `[base]` file, failed gates end in `failed` with the
324	report in `gate_report`.
325	
326	**G. Database and runner (S).** Migration `0004` with the new columns. `runner.py`
327	handles the `exists` outcome and stores `agent_sessions` and `gate_report`.
328	`retry` resumes the session. `POST /worlds` answers 409 with the world id for an
329	exact slug match.
330	
331	**H. Launcher and play route (M).** `launcher.py`: `ProcessLauncher`
332	(free port, spawn, `/healthz` wait, stop); `play.py` returns a "starting" page
333	that retries instead of the placeholder when the world is slow to boot. Tests
334	with a tiny stub server.
335	
336	**I. Website generation progress (S).** `WorldDetail.tsx` `STEPS` becomes
337	`check_exists`, `design`, `copy_template`, `fill`, `tests`, `polish`, `smoke`, `publish`,
338	with a per-file and per-test-round detail line; an "already exists" card with a
339	link to `duplicate_of`; `StatusChip` handles `exists`; catalogue card shows the
340	thumbnail. Update `PromptWindow` copy.
341	
342	**J. Deployment (S).** API image gets Node, `opencode`, the shared Python and
343	`node_modules` environment, Chromium for thumbnails; `compose.yaml` passes
344	`GEMINI_API_KEY` and the generator settings; `.env.example` documents them;
345	README gets a section.
346	
347	**K. End to end (M).** Add the `polish` step (Playwright screenshots, critique
348	prompt). Generate three different prompts, fix the template and
349	prompts where the agent gets stuck, record time and tokens per world and check the 5-minute budget. *Done
350	when:* a new world appears on the site, passes all gates and plays at all three
351	levels in a browser.
352	
353	**L. Hardening (L, after the demo).** Container per generation with an egress
354	allow-list, `test_run.py` with the Gemini player, agent
355	vs. you in the same world.
356	
357	Order: A first; B, C, D, E in parallel (different files); then F, G, H, I; then
358	J and K. Cut line for the demo: A–K.
359	
360	## Consequences
361	
362	- Quality comes from the template, `demand.py` and the gates more than from the
363	  prompt; a world is live only if the gates are green.
364	- Step order is code, so the agent cannot skip checks and single steps can be
365	  retried.
366	- The agent writes less per world, since levels are a table and demand is a
367	  config, which fits a Flash-class model.
368	- Template changes (levels in the URL, single port) do not
369	  reach worlds generated earlier.
370	
371	## Alternatives considered
372	
373	- **PydanticAI loop around Gemini instead of OpenCode:** more code to own
374	  (tools, edit format, retries); kept as the fallback.
375	- **OpenCode wrapped in PydanticAI:** two loops for one job.
376	- **Agent runs the whole workflow from one prompt:** it can skip the exists
377	  check, edit tests, or claim success without running anything.
378	- **One generation per level:** three rule sets drift apart and cost three times
379	  as much.
380	- **Free-form demand formulas:** break the playability gates and are hard to
381	  review.
382	- **`pixi install` per world:** minutes on first play.
383	- **Store worlds in the database:** code is a folder tree that tests and servers
384	  need on disk.
385	
386	## Open questions
387	
388	- Exact Gemini model ID and its speed: it decides whether 5 minutes is enough.
389	- Whether OpenCode's event stream is detailed enough (decided by the spike).
390	- Whether the budget table holds once measured (step K).
391	- Whether the Gemini critique in `polish` catches real layout problems; if not, replace it with fixed geometric checks (overlap, bounds).
392	
393	## Supersedes
394	
395	None

content.text:
The full plan is in `docs/design-decisions/0005-create-worlds-with-a-sandboxed-coding-agent.md` (396 lines, uncommitted, on branch `feat/world-creation-agent`). Here it is in condensed form.

## Goal
You enter a name and a description. A Gemini Flash coding agent builds a world with **3 difficulty levels (Easy, Medium, Hard)** in at most **5 minutes**. Tests must pass, then the world appears on the site and a human can play it. It all runs locally.

## Pipeline
The backend runs these steps in a fixed order, and the agent only does the creative ones.

| # | Step | Who | What happens |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `check_exists` | backend, then one Gemini call | Slug match in the DB and on disk, then a semantic comparison with existing worlds. A match ends the run as `exists` and links to that world. |
| 2 | `design` | agent | Writes `design.md`: story, hidden rules, demand factors, level table, `ui_state` shape, visual concept. |
| 3 | `copy_template` | backend | Copies the template to `src/worlds/<id>/` and stores `[base]` checksums. |
| 4 | `fill` | 2 agent sessions in parallel | `sim` writes `rules`, `env`, `demand_config`, `mcp`, `test_rules`. `ui` writes `World.tsx`. |
| 5 | `tests` | backend runs the gates, agent fixes | Up to 2 fix rounds. |
| 6 | `polish` | agent | Playwright screenshots, Gemini critique, one fix round. |
| 7 | `smoke` | backend | Builds the UI, boots the world, checks `/api/state`, MCP and `/`. |
| 8 | `publish` | backend | Writes `world.json` and `thumbnail.png`, sets `path` and `status=ready`. |

The agent can only write the allow-listed `[gen]` files. The backend compares `[base]` checksums before `tests` and `publish`, so the agent can't weaken a test.

## Agent loop
- OpenCode is the loop. There is no PydanticAI wrapper, because that would add a second loop for the same job. PydanticAI stays for the playing agent only.
- The backend starts `opencode serve` in the world folder and drives it over HTTP with `httpx`. A small Node script is the fallback if the HTTP API is awkward.
- The agent has permissions for edits to allow-listed paths and bash for tests only.
- Each OpenCode session's events are mapped to progress events for the website.
- The spike must verify all of this, because I haven't run OpenCode yet.

## Levels and demand
- Levels are cumulative and come from one table in `sim/env.py`. Level 3 is the expert mode: all demand factors, 3+ interacting hidden rules, fog, and noise.
- A new `sim/demand.py` implements the multiplicative demand model from your screenshot.
- The agent only writes `sim/demand_config.py`: which factors exist, their parameters, and the first level that enables each.
- Probed factors show up as "found" in Discoveries.

## Template changes
- **Levels:** `LEVELS` map, and `reset` by level.
- **Serving:** `/healthz`, the built UI served at `/`, SSE events, and a relative-URL UI with `?level=`.
- **Demand:** the new `demand.py` and `demand_config.py`.
- **Tests:** Vitest plus a frontend render test, which is listed in decision 0003 but doesn't exist yet, and the three new gates below.
- **Docs and tooling:** the visual checklist in `kit/README.md`, new `pixi` tasks, and README and brief updates.
- One global `Game` per world, because only one player plays at a time locally.

## Gates
- `check_env` and determinism per level.
- Contract, MCP and API checks.
- **New** playability: the baseline scores between 0 and 1, and gets worse as the level rises.
- **New** no-leak: hidden rules never appear in the brief or state.
- **New** demand sanity.
- `tsc`, `vite build`, and the Vitest render.
- Smoke boot.

## 5-minute budget (hard cap)
| Phase | Target | Cut-off |
|---|---|---|
| exists + design | 30 s | 45 s |
| fill (parallel) | 2 min | 2 min 30 s |
| tests | 1 min | 2 rounds, 1 min 15 s |
| polish | 30 s | 1 round, 45 s |
| smoke + publish | 30 s | 30 s |
| **Total** | **about 4 min** | **5 min, then `failed`** |

If the deadline passes, the partial world stays on disk and retry gets a fresh 5 minutes. Polish is the first thing skipped. I'm not sure this fits, because I don't know the model's speed. The end-to-end step measures it.

## Routing and storage
- Routing needs no per-world configuration. `/api/play/<id>/?level=N` goes through nginx to the API, which looks up the DB row, starts the world on demand, and proxies to its port. No load balancer is needed.
- A new `ProcessLauncher` starts each world from one shared prebuilt Python environment, so nothing is installed per world.
- The DB holds metadata only, plus new columns `duplicate_of`, `agent_sessions`, `model`, `gen_seconds` and `gate_report`, and the event log. The code lives in `src/worlds/<id>/`.
- The website never renders a world. It shows a catalogue card with a thumbnail and three Play links, which open the world's own UI in a new tab.

## Implementation steps
- **A. Spike (S):** drive OpenCode from Python and print its events.
- **B. Template (M):** levels, healthz, static UI, SSE.
- **C. Demand and gates (M):** `demand.py`, three new gates, Vitest.
- **D. Reference world (S):** move `bike-factory` to a committed `src/worlds-reference/`, updated to the new contract.
- **E. Website (S):** three levels across `DifficultySection`, `PromptWindow`, `ExistingWorlds`, `WorldDetail`, `PlayLevels`, their tests, and `LEVELS` and `le=3` in the backend.
- **F. Generator package (L):** `opencode_generator`, client, exists check, gates, prompts, settings.
- **G. DB and runner (S):** migration `0004`, the `exists` outcome, retry that resumes sessions.
- **H. Launcher (M):** `ProcessLauncher` and a "starting" page.
- **I. Progress UI (S):** new steps, an exists card, and thumbnails.
- **J. Deployment (S):** Node, `opencode`, the shared environment, Chromium, env vars.
- **K. End to end (M):** polish step, three real prompts, and measuring the 5-minute budget.
- **L. Hardening (L):** after the demo.

Order: A first, then B, C, D, E in parallel, then F, G, H, I, then J and K. The demo cut line is A–K.

## Open questions
- Exact Gemini model ID and speed.
- Whether OpenCode's event stream is rich enough, which the spike decides.
- Whether the Gemini critique in `polish` catches real layout problems. If not, it gets replaced with fixed geometric checks.

I spotted one small leftover: the pipeline table still says "max `N` rounds" for `tests`, and it should say 2.

Do you want me to fix that and commit the doc, or start on step A, the OpenCode spike?

"""[base] The world is a real planning problem: a baseline helps, and harder levels are not easier."""

import numpy as np
import pytest

from sim.helpers import world

Env = world()
SEEDS = range(10)


def _final_score(difficulty: str, seed: int, noop: bool = False) -> float:
    env = Env(difficulty)
    env.reset(seed=seed)
    done = False
    while not done:
        action = env.encode_actions([]) if noop else env.baseline_action()
        _, _, terminated, truncated, _ = env.step(action)
        done = terminated or truncated
    return env.score()["score"]


def _mean(difficulty: str, noop: bool = False) -> float:
    return float(np.mean([_final_score(difficulty, s, noop) for s in SEEDS]))


@pytest.fixture(params=Env.DIFFICULTIES)
def difficulty(request) -> str:
    return request.param


def test_baseline_scores_strictly_between_0_and_1(difficulty):
    for seed in SEEDS:

"""[base] Hidden rules stay hidden: nothing from secret.md reaches the agent or the UI."""

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from server.api import Game
from sim.helpers import world

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
Env = world()


def _secret_terms() -> set[str]:
    """Distinctive words in secret.md: backticked names and numbers with a unit, minus brief.md words."""
    secret = (ROOT / "secret.md").read_text()
    hidden = secret.split("## Scoring")[0]
    terms = {t.lower() for t in re.findall(r"`([^`]{4,})`", hidden)}
    brief = (ROOT / "brief.md").read_text().lower()
    return {t for t in terms if t not in brief}


@pytest.fixture(params=Env.DIFFICULTIES)
def game(request) -> Game:
    return Game(seed=11, difficulty=request.param)


def test_secret_terms_are_not_in_the_brief():
    brief = (ROOT / "brief.md").read_text().lower()
    assert not [t for t in _secret_terms() if t in brief]


def test_secret_terms_never_reach_observations_or_state(game):
    terms = _secret_terms()
    done = False
    while not done:
        seen = json.dumps([game.observe(), game.state(), game.score()]).lower()
        leaked = [t for t in terms if t in seen]
        assert not leaked, f"leaked: {leaked}"
        done = game.advance(1)["done"]


def test_hidden_demand_rules_start_hidden(game):
    """Before anything happens no factor text is revealed in the UI state."""
    assert game.state()["discoveries"]["found"] == []

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable
from contextlib import AbstractAsyncContextManager, asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
import pytest
from asgi_lifespan import LifespanManager
from planworldsimulator_backend.config import Settings
from planworldsimulator_backend.main import create_app


@asynccontextmanager
async def running_app(tmp_path: Path, **overrides) -> AsyncIterator[httpx.AsyncClient]:
    options = {
        "database_url": f"sqlite+aiosqlite:///{tmp_path / 'test.db'}",
        "worlds_dir": tmp_path / "worlds",
        "template_dir": tmp_path / "template",
        "step_delay_seconds": 0,
        # Tests create many worlds; the limits get their own dedicated tests.
        "create_limit_per_hour": 1000,
        "max_generating": 50,
        "seed_featured": False,
    }
    options.update(overrides)
    app = create_app(Settings(**options))
    async with LifespanManager(app):
        transport = httpx.ASGITransport(app=app)
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(

"""Prompt templates (generator/prompts/*.md) filled with the world's own files."""

import re
from pathlib import Path
from string import Template

PROMPTS = Path(__file__).parent / "prompts"
DEMAND_API_MARKERS = ("def ", "class ", "@dataclass", '"""')


def render(name: str, **values: str) -> str:
    return Template((PROMPTS / f"{name}.md").read_text()).safe_substitute(values)


def read(world_dir: Path, rel: str) -> str:
    return (world_dir / rel).read_text()


def fenced(world_dir: Path, rel: str) -> str:
    lang = {".py": "python", ".tsx": "tsx", ".md": "markdown"}.get(Path(rel).suffix, "")
    return f"### {rel}\n```{lang}\n{read(world_dir, rel).rstrip()}\n```"


def demand_api(world_dir: Path) -> str:
    """Signatures and docstrings of sim/demand.py without the function bodies."""
    out: list[str] = []
    keep = False
    for line in read(world_dir, "sim/demand.py").splitlines():
        if re.match(r"(def |class |@dataclass)", line):
            keep = True
            out.append(line)
        elif keep and (line.startswith(" ") or not line.strip()):
            if line.strip().startswith(('"""', "#")) or line.startswith("    ") and not line.startswith("     "):
                if line.strip().startswith('"""') or line.strip().startswith("#"):
                    out.append(line)
        else:
            keep = False
    return "```python\n" + "\n".join(out).rstrip() + "\n```"


def section(markdown: str, heading: str) -> str:
    """The text under `## heading` (until the next `## `), or an empty string."""
    match = re.search(rf"^## {re.escape(heading)}\s*\n(.*?)(?=^## |\Z)", markdown, re.S | re.M)
    return match.group(1).strip() if match else ""


REQUIRED_DESIGN_SECTIONS = (
    "Storyline", "Sites", "Actions", "Hidden rules", "Demand", "Levels", "Scoring",
    "UI state", "Visual concept",
)


def missing_sections(markdown: str) -> list[str]:
    return [h for h in REQUIRED_DESIGN_SECTIONS if not section(markdown, h)]

async def name_owner(sessions, title: str, exclude_id: str | None = None) -> str | None:
    """The id of an existing world with the same name (failed worlds do not count)."""
    from sqlalchemy import select

    from planworldsimulator_backend.db.models import World

    wanted = slug(title)
    async with sessions() as session:
        rows = await session.execute(
            select(World.id, World.title).where(World.status != "failed")
        )

        if world_id != exclude_id and slug(other) == wanted:
            return world_id
    return None
